toegepas.rede_vinder: Afrikaans waters a plant or tree with 'natgooi'; 'natmaak' just means to make wet. The protected 'kan maklik doodgaan' is untouched.
toegepas.fout: 'natmaak' is the loose verb; Afrikaans waters a tree or plant with the fixed verb 'natgooi'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Natgooi' is the precise, idiomatic verb for watering a tree, the meaning is unchanged, and the protected 'kan maklik doodgaan' is left intact.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'n regte verskil' calques English 'a real difference'; 'werklike' is the natural Afrikaans word with the same meaning and length.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'n Regte verskil maak' is natural, plain Afrikaans for a Grade 4 reader; 'werklike' is a lateral swap, not a fix.

laat_vaar.blok: Dinge wat jy elke dag kan doen
laat_vaar.voor: Maak kompos van skille en blare en spaar water
laat_vaar.na: Maak kompos van skille en blare, en spaar water
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Two separate commands are joined by 'en' right after the list 'skille en blare'; the comma separates the two clauses so the child does not read 'spaar water' as a third thing compost is made of.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Under AWS 2017 two command halves with no stated subject of their own take no comma before 'en', so the original punctuation is correct.

laat_vaar.voor: Suid-Afrika hou elke jaar in die eerste week van September Nasionale Boomplantweek.
laat_vaar.na: Suid-Afrika hou Nasionale Boomplantweek elke jaar in die eerste week van September.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The long time phrase in front of the object makes the sentence heavy; naming the week first reads more naturally with the same words.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Putting the time phrase before the object is normal Afrikaans word order and the sentence already reads well; the reorder is a lateral move.

vlae.rede: The block heading still says 'Boomplantdag', while the block itself says the day has become Nasionale Boomplantweek. A heading cannot be changed by the language step; the writer may want the heading and the text to name the same thing.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Vullis wat lê waar dit nie hoort nie
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: waar vullis beland waar dit nie hoort nie
laat_vaar_vorige.na: waar vullis beland wat nie daar hoort nie
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Avoids the clumsy 'waar ... waar' repetition without changing the meaning or the length.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Waar ... waar' is acceptable, and the restrictive 'vullis wat nie daar hoort nie' quietly suggests some litter does belong there; it also breaks the parallel with the heading and the glossary wording.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Vuil water kan 'n mens maagsiek maak
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: lyk soms skoon en is dit tog nie
laat_vaar_vorige.na: lyk soms skoon maar is dit tog nie
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The sentence is a contrast, so 'maar' is the natural joiner; no comma because the second half shares the subject.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'En is dit tog nie' is natural Afrikaans, since 'tog' already carries the contrast; swapping in 'maar' is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'met 'n grootmens by' is a loose colloquial construction; 'saam met' is standard and keeps 'altyd' and the adult rule intact.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'met 'n grootmens by' is idiomatic Afrikaans for an adult being present, so this is a lateral move inside a safety instruction (who must be there), and that wording stays as checked.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: wat deur bome en plante opgeneem word
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'wat bome en plante opneem' can be read as the gas taking up the trees; the passive makes clear that the plants take up the gas.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: This is a glossary definition, and the reading the finder warns about (the gas taking up the trees) is too absurd to mislead anyone; the passive makes it longer and breaks the parallel with the 'suurstof' entry.
